To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
training induces upregulation of nuclear MMP-2 and cytoplasmic and nuclear MMP-9 in rat Sol muscle.
training activates nuclear and cytoplasmic gelatinases, and that the nuclear gelatinases may be involved in the control of gene expression.
intense exercise activates nuclear MMP- 2 and increases expression and activation of cytoplasmatic MMP-9 in Soleus, but not in Extensor digitorium longus muscle of rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of MMP-9 and MMP-2 activities in the muscle of control and exercised rats, and the possible role of these enzymes in muscle adaptation to exercise.
the study of the fine-structural distribution of the activities of the two gelatinases MMP2 and MMP9 in rat skeletal muscle, upon physical training.
the role of matrix metalloproteinase in skeletal muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gelatinolytically active MMP-2 and -9 are upregulated in skeletal muscle after training, and that this upregulation is associated with myonuclear and satellite cell functions, and myofiber remodeling.
the gelatinase activity in the myonucleus is associated with RNA Polymerase II and may play a role in myonucleus remodeling.
MMP-2 and -9 are upregulated by training, with the former being nuclear and the latter cytoplasmic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gelatinase activities in skeletal muscles are not constitutive, and are upregulated by intense exercise in the myonucleus and in the cytoplasma of myoblasts.
MMP-2 and/or MMP-9 are involved in muscle fiber adaptation to training.
the training-induced increase in MMP-2 and -9 activity in Sol muscle is associated with the activation of myonuclei and the proliferation of satellite cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gelatinolytically active MMP-2 is localized in the myonucleus and may be involved in the regulation of gene expression in muscle.
training-related upregulations of gelatinolytics occur in myonuclei and activated satellite cells/myotubes.
the gelatinolytically active form of MMPs is not restricted to the extracellular compartment, and that MMPs may be involved in the regulation of myonuclei and satellite cells.
